summary: Lebanon issues free one-month visas on arrival at Beirut airport to citizens of the EU, US, UK, Canada, Australia and many other countries — extendable to three months — while GCC nationals enter visa-free; other nationalities apply through a Lebanese embassy, and any traveler with evidence of travel to Israel is refused entry.

passportValidity.text: Carry a passport valid for at least 6 months on arrival — Lebanese border officials commonly apply the 6-month rule.

travelInsurance.text: Not required for entry, but strongly recommended. Check that your policy actually covers Lebanon, as many insurers exclude it while government advisories against travel are in force.

onwardTicket.text: Not systematically checked on arrival, but airlines may ask for a return or onward ticket before boarding.

source.name: Lebanese General Directorate of General Security

proofOfFunds.text: No fixed amount is published; border officers occasionally ask visitors to show means of support and an address in Lebanon.

source.name: Lebanese General Directorate of General Security

currencyLimits.text: Large amounts of cash should be declared on arrival — thresholds change; check with Lebanese customs before carrying more than about USD 15,000.

notes: Drones may not be brought in without prior authorization and are frequently confiscated at the airport.
Any item purchased in Israel or bearing Hebrew labeling can lead to questioning and refused entry.

payments.text: Since the financial crisis Lebanon runs largely on US dollar cash. Bring crisp USD notes, as cards and ATMs are unreliable and the pound's street value differs from posted rates.

safety.text: Lebanon's security situation is volatile: the 2023–2024 conflict with Israel and its aftermath left parts of the south, the Beqaa Valley and Beirut's southern suburbs high-risk, and many governments still advise against all or most travel. Conditions change quickly. Check your government's advice immediately before traveling.

bestTimeToVisit.text: April to June and September to October offer warm, dry weather for Beirut, the mountains and the coastal sites without the summer crowds or winter rain.

idp.text: Lebanon is a party to the 1949 Geneva Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1968 Vienna one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1949 Geneva version. A permit issued under the 1968 Vienna Convention carries no treaty obligation here.

driving.text: Lebanon is a party to the 1949 Geneva Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1968 Vienna one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1949 Geneva version. A permit issued under the 1968 Vienna Convention carries no treaty obligation here. Whether a permit is required in addition to a national license, and for how long a foreign license may be used, are set by national road law and have not been checked for Lebanon yet.

tips.text: Any evidence of travel to Israel — stamps, visas, Jordanian or Egyptian exit stamps from Israeli land borders, even Israeli-bought items — leads to refused entry and possible detention. Travel with a clean passport.

Avoid the southern border area, parts of the Beqaa Valley, Palestinian refugee camps and Beirut's southern suburbs, and monitor the news and your embassy's advice daily. The situation can deteriorate rapidly.
Bring the money you will need as US dollar cash in good-condition notes. Cards, ATMs and bank withdrawals are unreliable, and dollars are accepted almost everywhere.
State electricity runs only a few hours a day — hotels, restaurants and shops rely on private generators, so brief outages during switchover are normal.
The free one-month visa on arrival can be extended to three months at a General Security office. Start the process before the first month expires.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Lebanon?
faq.answer: Most Western travelers do not need to arrange anything in advance: citizens of the EU, UK, US, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Japan and many other countries receive a free one-month visa on arrival at Beirut airport, extendable to three months. GCC nationals enter visa-free. Other nationalities must apply at a Lebanese embassy before travel.

faq.question: Can I enter Lebanon if I have been to Israel?
faq.answer: No. Lebanon refuses entry to anyone whose passport or belongings show evidence of travel to Israel — stamps, visas, border-crossing stamps from Jordan or Egypt, or Israeli products. Israeli citizens are barred entirely. If you have visited Israel, travel on a new, clean passport and carry nothing linking you to the trip.

faq.question: Is Lebanon safe to visit right now?
faq.answer: It depends where and when. Beirut, the mountains and the northern coast function normally much of the time, but the security situation is genuinely volatile — many governments still advise against all or most travel, and areas near the Israeli border, parts of the Beqaa Valley and Beirut's southern suburbs are high-risk. Check current advisories immediately before booking and again before flying.

faq.question: How much does the Lebanese visa on arrival cost?
faq.answer: Nothing — the standard one-month single-entry tourist visa issued on arrival at Beirut airport is free for eligible nationalities. Extensions to three months are handled by General Security in Lebanon.

faq.question: What money should I bring to Lebanon?
faq.answer: US dollars in cash, in clean undamaged notes. Lebanon's banking system remains dysfunctional: foreign cards often fail, ATMs dispense pounds at unfavourable rates, and nearly every hotel, restaurant and shop accepts (and prefers) dollars. Small denominations are useful for daily spending.
